council_procurement_patterns._note: General intelligence gathered about how councils procure accessibility works. Update as you learn more.
council_procurement_patterns.dfg_route: Disabled Facilities Grants (DFG) are means-tested grants provided by local councils to help disabled people make adaptations to their homes. Occupational Therapists (OTs) assess needs; HIA (Home Improvement Agencies) and housing officers manage the grant. Suppliers often work via approved supplier lists.
council_procurement_patterns.approved_supplier_list: Many councils maintain an approved supplier list for DFG works. Getting on this list is the priority — it removes the need to win individual tenders.
council_procurement_patterns.direct_award: Below ~£25k many councils can direct-award without tender. Building relationships with DFG officers and OTs creates referral opportunities.
council_procurement_patterns.framework_contracts: Some councils use NEPO, YPO, or Crown Commercial Service frameworks. Worth investigating if SesameAccess qualifies.

what_works: Personal contact via named person from Contracts Finder notice → warm introduction
Apollo enrichment to find Portfolio/Project Managers who have broader council visibility
DFG officers as primary target — they directly specify adaptations
OTs as secondary target — they write adaptation reports that specify equipment
what_to_avoid: Generic procurement inboxes — low response rate
Emailing the same person multiple times within 90 days
Pitching passenger lift / shaft lift capability — not what SesameAccess does
Maintenance contract notices — not relevant to SesameAccess product offering
outreach_learnings.product_positioning: SesameAccess supplies disability access platform lifts, threshold lifts, and step-free access solutions — specifically for DFG-funded residential adaptations and public building accessibility works. NOT passenger elevator / shaft lift maintenance.
